risk_assessment.rationale: Office macros spawning hidden PowerShell with encoded commands is a well-established spearphishing and malware delivery technique that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code while evading basic detection. The decoded segment IEX (New-Object suggests download-and-execute behavior typical of malicious payloads. Confidence is medium because only two evidence events exist and domain enrichment for jtan-lt01.victimcorp.com and jane.tan is unknown, limiting context on user legitimacy and host history.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Isolate host jtan-lt01.victimcorp.com from network and capture memory dump before shutdown to preserve in-memory payloads and PowerShell artifacts.
Correlate the Excel file Invoice_2984773.xlsm with email gateway logs for user jane.tan to identify sender, attachment hash, and delivery timestamp.
Search enterprise telemetry for other executions of powershell.exe with -Enc from Office processes across all endpoints in last 30 days.
Obtain and detonate the XLSM file in sandbox to extract macros and confirm malicious intent and C2 infrastructure.
triage_rationale_experimental: Encoded PowerShell spawned from a macro-enabled Excel is highly suspicious but enrichment is unknown and evidence count is only 2, so confirmation is needed before calling it a true positive.
